items.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: those were playing Benny Goodman and Tommy Dorsey and Jimmy Lunceford and Count Basie arrangements.

ctx.x: Well we heard a good selection of tunes last night with Jazz at the Philharmonic. You come from an area of the country that I think probably offered some jazz opportunity when you grew up.

Well I think one of the basic things that helped me was the school system, because I know in New York State and Pennsylvania and Michigan, they have, at least at that time, they had music in most of the schools, and this helps a great deal, those who want to be musicians because when we were in high school we had Harmony I, Harmony II, Theory I, Theory II, we had a marching band, we had a concert band, and there was tradition for an after school jazz band and those were playing Benny Goodman and Tommy Dorsey and…

so that was a great help and I was fortunately elected to be the director of the choir for the last two years, for just the high school. And I ended up being Class Musician. So this year, I came out in ‘46, and we’re having our fiftieth reunion this year, and I’m looking forward to it.
